prompt: A Service name resolves, direct Pod IP works from the client Pod, but ClusterIP times out. Diagnose and recover safely.
directAnswer: Bind context, source/destination Pod UIDs, nodes, five-tuple, Service UID and time. DNS and one application/listener path are proven. Inspect Service port/targetPort, selector, EndpointSlices with targetRef UIDs/readiness and the actual Service dataplane implementation. Test the VIP from same and different nodes, evaluate source egress/destination ingress policy and return path, and inspect bounded dataplane sync/drop evidence. Repair the owning Service, policy or node agent; verify the normal name/VIP path, multiple endpoints and served revision.
foundation: Direct endpoint success isolates later Service mapping/dataplane/policy boundaries.
reasoningSteps: State what DNS and direct Pod success prove.
Inspect actual dataplane mode and sync health.
Repair owner and verify normal user path.
seniorAnswer: I do not restart DNS or the application because their relevant boundaries succeeded. I inspect the Service contract, slice membership, proxy/replacement programming, policy and return path, preserve path-specific evidence, then make the smallest source-controlled correction and verify revision-aware traffic.
weakAnswer: Restart CoreDNS and every kube-proxy Pod.
whyWeak: DNS already answered and direct backend works; broad restarts risk availability and destroy evidence.
